Question Choices: A rectangle is 2/5m tall and 6/7 m wide. Find the area.
Hints: Multiply height by width. Metres times metres gives square metres.
Solution: 2/5 x 6/7 = (2/5) x (6/7) = 12/35. Simplified result: 12/35. Answer: 12/35 square metres.

Question Choices: Select. When a rectangle tall and wide are measure in meter (m). What unit should the area be measured in? ~~A | B~~
Solution: Area multiplies two lengths: m x m = m², square metres. The figure labels this choiceB.

Question Choices: If a rectangle is split into 5 equal rows and 6 equal columns, how many equal small rectangles are there total?
Hints: Multiply equal rows by columns to count all cells.
Solution: 5 equal rows x 6 equal columns=30 equal small rectangles.

Question Choices: A rectangle is 2 m tall and 5 m wide. It is split into 5 equal rows (tall) and 6 equal columns (wide). What are the tall and wide of each small rectangle? Give your answer as a number or fraction only. Do not write units.
Hints: Divide whole dimensions to find one cell; multiply cell dimensions to recover the whole.
Solution: Height = 2 / 5 = 2/5 m. Width = 5 / 6 = 5/6 m. Keep rows with height and columns with width.

Question Choices: A 1 m x 1 m large rectangle is divided into several equal rectangles. If each small rectangle is 1/40 of the whole square, what is the area of one small rectangle in square meter? Give your answer as a number or fraction only. Do not write units.
Hints: Find the whole area, then divide it equally among the stated number of parts.
Solution: The whole square has area 1 m x 1 m=1 square metre. Divide into 40 equal parts:1/40 square metre per part.

Question Choices: A 1 m x 1 m square is divided into 8 columns and 7 rows, as shown. A shaded rectangle covers 7 columns and 5 rows. What fraction of the whole is shaded?
Hints: Count shaded rows times shaded columns and divide by total rows times total columns.
Solution: The figure shows 8 columns and 7 rows:56 tiles. The shaded region covers 7 columns and 5 rows:35 tiles. Shaded fraction 35/56=5/8.

Question Choices: The large rectangle is 1m tall and 5 m wide. It is divided into 18 equal small rectangles as above. What is the area of the shaded area in square meter? Give your answer as a number or fraction only. Do not write units
Hints: Find the whole area, then multiply by the shaded fraction.
Solution: Whole area 1 x 5=5 square metres. The figure shows 3 rows x 6 columns=18 tiles, with 3 x 4=12 shaded. Shaded area 5 x 12/18=10/3=3 1/3 square metres.

Question Choices: A large rectangle is equally divided to 24 small rectangles as above. Each small rectangle is 1/2 m tall and 2/7 m wide. What are the height and width of the large rectangle? Give your answer as a number or fraction only. Do not write units
Hints: Divide whole dimensions to find one cell; multiply cell dimensions to recover the whole.
Solution: Height = 1/2 x 4 = 2 m. Width = 2/7 x 6 = 1 5/7 m. Keep rows with height and columns with width.

Question Choices: A large rectangle is equally divided to 24 small rectangles as above. Each small rectangle is 1/2 m tall and 2/7 m wide. What is the area of large rectangle? Give your answer as a number or fraction only. Do not write units
Hints: Find one tile area, then multiply by the whole or shaded tile count.
Solution: One tile area=(1/2)x(2/7)=1/7 square metre. Whole area=24 x 1/7=3 3/7 square metres.

Question Choices: A large rectangle is equally divided to 21 small rectangles. Each small rectangle is 2/5 m tall and 3/8 m wide. What is the area of large rectangle? What is the area of shaded part? Give your answer as a number or fraction only. Do not write units
Hints: Find one tile area, then multiply by the whole or shaded tile count.
Solution: One tile area=(2/5)x(3/8)=3/20 square metre. Whole area=21 x 3/20=3 3/20 square metres. Shaded area=4 x 3/20=3/5 square metre(s).
